title: Autosharded token-cap batching with deadline-slicing and speculative hedging for reranker endpoint
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The rerank endpoint has observed P50 improvements from existing batching work but P95/P99 tail remains volatile during mixed short/long token workloads and high concurrency. We need a coherent approach that: 1) bounds per-request token work to avoid single long requests blocking batch progress, 2) parallelizes safe work across lanes while preserving model cache locality, and 3) provides graceful timeouts/hedging so SLOs are met without excessive cost.
proposal_summary: Implement an autosharding layer that splits long candidate lists into token-capped shards at enqueue time, run shards in parallel on separated microbatch lanes, and coordinate a deadline-aware timebox that cancels or hedges remaining shards to fallback ranker variants. Add KV prefetch cancellation: prefetch once per shard group, cancel in-flight prefetches when a fast lane determines the final top-K. Provide runtime knobs per-tenant and per-route (token_cap, max_shards, lane_count, deadline_ms, hedge_threshold_ms).
design_decisions:
- Use deterministic shard boundaries (by candidate index) to preserve rerank determinism across retries.
- Prefer parallel microbatch lanes pinned to different GPU streams within the same serving host to reduce cross-host coordination.
- Maintain a ‘fast-pass’ lane that runs with aggressive token_cap and short deadline to capture low-latency responses; full-pass lanes run in background for quality and are only used if fast-pass confidence is low.
- KV prefetch will be batched per-shard-group and exposed as a cancellable future to avoid wasted memory/IO.
- Default tenant settings conservative: token_cap=256, max_shards=4, lane_count=3, deadline_ms=120 for fast-pass. Tunable via route config.
acceptance_criteria:
- P95 latency for rerank requests (standard test rig) improves by >= 15% compared to baseline under mixed short/long workload.
- 99th percentile tail reduction >= 8% without increasing median cost by > 10%.
- No regressions in top-k quality (MAP@10) > 0.5% vs baseline on acceptance prompt set.
- Feature is configurable per-route and has an opt-out toggle.
- End-to-end observability: per-shard latency, lane utilization, KV-prefetch cancellation rate, hedged-fallback rate, and cost delta surfaces in Console.
rollout_plan: 1) Spike/proof-of-concept in the staging cluster (done). 2) Canary: enable on 2 internal routes (low-traffic) with token_cap=128 and lane_count=2 for 48 hours; monitor latency/cost/quality. 3) Gradual ramp to 5% production traffic with auto rollback on SLA breach alerts. 4) Enable per-tenant opt-in in Console and expose detailed metrics before wider rollout.
observability_plan: Add metrics: rerank.shard.count, rerank.shard.latency.{p50,p95,p99}, rerank.lane.utilization, rerank.kv.prefetch.cancel_rate, rerank.hedge.invocations, rerank.fallback_rate, rerank.cost.tokens_per_request. Hook traces into existing request-id tracing; add dashboards for per-route comparison and a canary alert rule tied to P99 and fallback_rate.
tradeoffs:
- Parallelizing shards increases peak GPU memory and potential kernel contention; mitigated by lane_count limits and token caps.
- Hedging/fast-pass may slightly lower top-K quality for some pathological queries; we keep full-pass as a fallback to preserve quality but it can increase cost.
- Prefetch cancellation reduces wasted I/O but adds complexity and potential for race conditions; careful testing required.
spike_results: Staging simulation (mixed workload: 70% short 16 tokens, 30% long 1024 tokens) with token_cap=256 and lane_count=3: median latency unchanged, P95 reduced by 18%, P99 reduced by 9%. Cost increase observed +6% tokens/request. KV prefetch cancel_rate ~34% and reduced GPU memory pressure by ~12% in the fast-pass scenario.
implementation_notes:
- Server changes: enqueue-time shardizer, lane scheduler, cancellable prefetch futures, per-request deadline manager.
- Runtime config: add route-level policy and tenant defaults in control plane.
- SDK: expose hints (max_shards) and new response metadata (shard_count, hedged=true/false, fallback_reason).
- Tests: unit tests for shardizer determinism, e2e latency bench harness, long-running soak test for memory leak detection.

2026-03-07: Design review with Applied ML (lead: Priya Rao) — agreed fast-pass confidence metric thresholding; updated acceptance criteria to include MAP@10 guardrail.
